title: Minimum Swaps to Make Strings Equal
summary: Given two strings s1 and s2 of equal length containing only 'x' and 'y', determine the minimum swaps needed to make both strings identical.
statement: Given two strings s1 and s2 of equal length containing only 'x' and 'y', determine the minimum swaps needed to make both strings identical. Swaps must involve characters from different strings. Return -1 if equalization is impossible.
constraints: Strings have equal length and contain only x and y.
One swap exchanges characters at different positions across the two strings.
hints: Count xy and yx mismatch orientations.
Two equal orientations cost one swap; one leftover of each costs two.
An odd total mismatch count is impossible.
Pairing identical orientations is optimal, leaving at most one mixed pair.
editorial: Pairing identical orientations is optimal, leaving at most one mixed pair.

tests.explanation: Two xy mismatches are fixed by one cross-string swap.
Opposite mismatch types require two swaps.
